newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki stays close to home pre-FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki stays close to home pre-FOMC.

text.p: Share trade dragged to a halt on Tuesday with the index hugging tight margins as operators waited to see if the U.S. Federal Reserve hikes rates at a key meeting. Some brokers voiced fears of a correction whatever the outcome.

"Everyone is waiting for direction from New York, but prices are a bit high right now," one said, adding: "When you look at how strong the rise has been since the beginning of the year, it's now a question of keeping up that performance."
The HEX index, which scraped a 0.2 percent increase on the day to end at 3,035.14, has put on over 20 percent since end-96. An early dip in U.S. stocks fuelled brokers' nerves.
Forestry group Enso and paper machine maker Valmet provided the sole highlights: "Without the Valmet and Enso news, this would have been a terribly dull day," one broker said.

Enso put on an early spurt after its Q1 report came in well above market expectations, touching a year-high of 49.80 markka. But amid general caution buying momentum soon failed, and it closed up just 0.90 at 46.90 in unremarkable volumes.
Valmet managed more sustained action after saying it won a big machine order from Norske Skog, ending up 0.50 markka at 88.50 and accounting for eight percent of total trade.
